name: Alphecca
description: A subgiant of type A1 IV 23.7 parsecs away, 3.9 times the Sun's width: its disc was measured with the Navy Precision Optical Interferometer.

radius.source: Baines et al. (2025), AJ 169, 293, HD 139006: radius 3.88 +/- 0.11 solar radii (Table 7), from the limb-darkened angular diameter 1.525 +/- 0.027 mas (NPOI, Table 6) and the Gaia DR3 (Gaia Collaboration 2022) parallax

temperature.source: Baines et al. (2025), AJ 169, 293, HD 139006: effective temperature 8152 +/- 93 K (Table 7), from the angular diameter and the bolometric flux of the SED fit

gravity.source: Baines et al. (2025), AJ 169, 293, HD 139006: log g 3.82, from Allende Prieto & Lambert (1999), as the paper lists it beside the diameter (Table 6)

distance.source: Baines et al. (2025), AJ 169, 293, HD 139006: the Gaia DR3 (Gaia Collaboration 2022) parallax the radius was computed with (Table 2), 42.24 +/- 0.98 mas, inverted

text.card: A subgiant of type A1 IV, 24 parsecs away: 3.9 times the Sun's width.
text.introduction: Its disc spans 1.525 milliarcseconds, which gives 3.88 solar radii and 8,152 K at its surface.
text.locator: Tables 2, 6 and 7, HD 139006: parallax, MK type, limb-darkened diameter, radius, Teff

radialVelocity.source: SIMBAD's radial velocity for Gaia DR3 1222646935698492160 (quality E), from 1953GCRV..C......0W; Gaia DR3 measures none
